source_text: Sed videamus et reliqua. Postquam ergo dixisti: Haec forma non omni ex parte conformis est, adiungis: Unde hic Apostolus secutus adiunxit: " Sed non sicut delictum ita et donatio; si enim ob unius delictum multi mortui sunt, multo magis gratia Dei et donum in gratia unius hominis Iesu Christi in plures abundavit " [n125] . Quam sententiam hoc modo exponis: Quid est: " multo magis abundavit ", nisi quia omnes, qui per Christum liberantur, temporaliter propter Adam moriuntur, propter ipsum autem Christum sine fine victuri sunt? [n126] Pronuntiavit certe Apostolus, de cuius nobis est opinione certamen, efficacius operari ad collationem salutis et copiosius gratiam Salvatoris quam peccatum Adae, ut ostenderet multo vehementius profuisse Christum et pluribus profuisse, cuius gratia, ut ipso eius verbo utar: abundavit in plures, quam praevaricationem primi hominis nocuisse, quem tu dicis seminibus illigasse peccatum.
pass_a_gloss: But let us see also the remaining things. After therefore you said: This form is not conformed from every part, you add: Whence here the Apostle, having followed, added: 'But not as the offense so also the donation; for if on account of the offense of one many died, much more the grace of God and the gift in the grace of one human being Jesus Christ abounded unto more.' Which sentence you explain in this way: What is: 'it abounded much more,' except because all who are freed through Christ die temporally on account of Adam, but on account of Christ himself they are about to live without end? The Apostle, about whose meaning there is a contest for us, certainly pronounced that the Savior's grace works more effectively toward the conferring of salvation and more copiously than Adam's sin, so that he might show that Christ helped much more vehemently and helped more people, whose grace, to use his own word: abounded unto more, than the transgression of the first human being harmed, which you say bound sin into seeds.

lemmas.lexica: LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin
LS praevaricatio; Blaise Adam's transgression as example
LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS donum; Blaise grace-gift vs inherited sin
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: But let us examine the rest. After saying, ‘This figure does not correspond in every respect,’ you add: ‘Therefore the apostle went on to add here: “But the gift is not like the offense. For if through the one man’s offense many died, much more did God’s grace and the gift in the grace of the one man Jesus Christ abound to more people”’ (Romans 5:15). You explain this statement as follows: ‘What does “abound much more” mean, except that everyone freed through Christ dies a temporal death on account of Adam, but will live without end on account of Christ himself?’ (Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.46). The apostle, whose meaning we are disputing, certainly declared that the Savior’s grace works more effectively and abundantly to confer salvation than Adam’s sin works against it. He thus showed that Christ helped far more powerfully, and helped more people—his grace, to use the apostle’s own expression, ‘abounded to more people’—than were harmed by the first man’s transgression, which you say bound sin into human seed.

variants.reading: The comparative “more people” renders the Latin plures used in Julian’s quotation and argument; it is not substituted from a modern Bible translation.
